SPXW options priced ±1.17% for today from Wednesday's 7,182.78 close, a top near 7,267. Perps near 7,282 already sit above it.

means: Perps near 7,282 sit above 7,267, the top of today's ±1.17% implied move, and above the 7,201 trigger. The gap already uses all of the priced move.
The wider trade gap did not move perps: 7,297 at 8:29am, 7,296 at 8:45am. Since then perps eased to 7,282.
Memory leads again: Sandisk, WDC and Micron perps +5% to +10%. Holding that after 9:30am keeps the rebound led by the hardest hit names.
Back under 7,201 reopens the 7,060 to 7,200 range; a full gap fill is 7,183. The cash close is 1:00pm with thin books.

qa: Why are stocks set to open higher?
Yahoo says semis rose as nerves over AI profitability eased, and TokenPost says selling in AI stocks paused. S&P perp +1.4% and Nasdaq 100 perp +2.1% vs Wednesday.
The October goods deficit widened to $149.5B vs $133.1B expected as imports jumped 6.1%. Wholesale inventories rose 0.9% vs 0.5% expected.
Not visibly: the S&P perp was 7,297 at 8:29am and 7,296 at 8:45am. It has since eased to 7,282.
CME FedWatch shows a 98.9% chance of a 25bp hike on Dec 9. Odds of 50bp of hikes by January were 58.4% on Wednesday.
From Wednesday's close SPXW options priced ±1.17% for today and ±2.73% through Dec 4. Puts at 25 delta trade at 31% IV vs 26% at the money for Dec 4.
What happened in Korea and Japan?
Kospi closed +4.34% and the Nikkei +2.11%; Shanghai rose 3.7% after China signaled market support. Japanese chip equipment led.
TrendForce sees NAND contract prices −0% to −5% in 1Q27 as Chinese cloud buyers cut SSD orders, and cut its 2027 DRAM outlook. HBM and server DRAM stay the tightest.
The trade data printed wider than expected and perps eased about 0.1%. Brent is near $92 on Yahoo and the perp, below the $97.62 cited earlier.
